name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans Republican by roughly 22 points
Griffith outraises Powers about nine to one with over $1 million on hand
No polls or expert ratings indicate a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Griffith's commanding fundraising advantage, and the absence of any polling or expert ratings suggesting competition all point to a comfortable incumbent win; even a Democratic-leaning national environment falls well short of what Powers would need.
model.watch: A strong national Democratic wave could narrow the margin, but the seat would remain out of reach absent a historic shift in this part of Virginia.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Virginia's 9th District spans the state's southwestern coalfields and mountain counties, one of the most Republican-leaning seats in Virginia. Morgan Griffith has held the seat since 2011 and enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised roughly nine times as much as Democrat Joy Powers and holding more than $1 million on hand. No public polling tracks the race, and expert raters have not listed it as competitive.

The district's partisan lean of about 22 points toward Republicans would require an extraordinary shift for Powers to contend. Prediction markets put Griffith's chances near 97 percent. Even in a favorable midterm environment for Democrats, the combination of incumbency, geography, and the money gap makes this a Safe Republican seat, with the main question being the size of Griffith's winning margin.
